The down_proj-only half fails the criterion. It gives only 55% of C's onset effect (−0.24 against −0.44; P_onset 0.645 against 0.596) but keeps 77% of the flip proxy (0.67% against 0.87%). So the MLP half is the less selective part. Taken at face value, this hints that the attention (o_proj) half carries a comparable onset effect with much less collateral, perhaps 0.2–0.3% flips, though the halves need not add up.

I'll screen C_attn(−1.5), o_proj only in layers 16–22 (7 tensors), on the same texts. It passes if onset is ≤ −0.29 or P_onset ≤ 0.64 with flip ≤ 0.29%. If its onset effect is about −0.2 with a low flip proxy, a larger attention-only dose would be the natural candidate. With the 8 passes left after this, a generation test still fits: a DEV both-pass of 1,024 is 4 passes, and HOLDOUT gets the rest.

The current edit is now the o_proj-only half, C_attn(−1.5), in 7 tensors. This teacher-forced pass on screenL_texts completes the split. The criterion is the same: onset ≤ −0.29 or P_onset ≤ 0.64, with flip proxy ≤ 0.29%. A low flip proxy with an onset effect near −0.2 would motivate a larger attention-only dose. A flip proxy near 0.4% or above would close the module-split line.
The attention-only screen is done. Here is the same table with all three variants. C_attn passes if onset ≤ −0.29 or P_onset ≤ 0.64, with flip proxy ≤ 0.29%.

Neither half is cleaner than the whole. The attention-only half gives just 18% of C's onset effect (−0.08) while keeping 47% of its flip proxy (0.41%). The MLP-only half gives 55% of the onset effect with 77% of the flips. The full edit's onset effect (−0.44) is larger than the two halves combined (−0.32), so the halves reinforce each other through the residual stream, and C applied to both modules is the most selective option. I'm closing the module-split line and restoring nothing yet, because one dose question remains open.

Loop-freeing had already plateaued between β = 1.5 and 2.25, with the same cut share. The dose that frees most loops at the least collateral may lie below 1.5. I'll test C(−1.0), built the same way, on all of DEV (4 passes: dev_a1, dev_a2, dev_b1, dev_b2). The pre-registered rule: proceed to HOLDOUT (holdout_1, 2, 3, X1, 4 passes) only if pooled DEV gain is at least +1.9, i.e. 2 points above C(−1.5)'s DEV result of about −0.1 over 1,024. Then replace C(−1.5) only if C(−1.0) also matches or beats C(−1.5)'s +2.8 on those same 1,024 HOLDOUT problems. Otherwise the submission stays C(−1.5).
